newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqis start receiving additional food rations.
newsitem.headline: Iraqis start receiving additional food rations.

text.p: The Iraqi government began distributing additional food rations to its citizens on Sunday under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

Under the new rations, each Iraqi is entitled to a monthly quota of nine kg (20 lb) of flour instead of seven kg (15.4 lb), 2.5 kg (6 lb) of rice instead of 1.25 and one kilo (2.2 lb) of cooking oil instead of 650 grams. Rations of goods like soap and detergent powder will be increased about 50 per cent.

Rations of sugar and tea have not increased yet under the oil deal, which allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"There has been no contract of sugar approved yet except one with a French firm which is about 20,000 tonnes," the spokesman for the U.N. coordinator in Iraq, Eric Falt, told Reuters.
Iraq complained on Sunday to visiting U.N. Under-Secretary General Yasushi Akashi about delays in approving food and medicine contracts by the U.N. sanctions committee.

Falt said the U.N. sanctions committee had approved 143 contracts and about 500,000 tonnes of foodstuffs had reached Iraq. More than 120 international U.N. observers supervise the arrival, storage and distribution of food.
